panels.observation: Source P1 Panel 1 caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' is used word for word as narration. It names Dr. Ananya for the reader and depends on no earlier text.

Meera's source line is word for word, split at the ellipsis into two balloons by the same speaker ('Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' / 'I wish everything were easier to manage!'). No turn is skipped. The phone and registers in the scene set up the list.
Ananya's 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' is word for word. 'the rest' refers back to Meera's 01-2 list, which comes just before it.

The caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' is word for word. The label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' is a manga supplement naming the product the source panel shows. It reads after the caption.
'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' is word for word, and Ananya is the speaker, as in the source. 'here' is backed by the 02-1 laptop setup.
Meera's 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' is word for word. 'And' continues Ananya's 02-2 line directly, with no speaker in between. The WELBUK CARE label is a supplement.
Ananya's 'One team. Better coordination.' is word for word and sums up 02-2 and 02-3. Meera only nods, with no added line.

Revised P3 Panel 1 caption 'The front desk is always an option.' is word for word, and the textColumns join exactly. With no spoken line, the scene (Meera checking in an elderly patient) carries 'front desk'. This follows the stated time change from 02-4 and the evening onboarding.

Caption 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' is word for word. 'Some' contrasts with the front desk option in 03-1. It is the first mention of Welbuk Health; the label naming the product comes later in 06-2.
Caption 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' is word for word and introduces Ravi by name for the first time. The QR stand in the scene backs 'at the door'.

Caption 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' is word for word. 'his' refers to Ravi in 03-3, and the consent tick-box in the scene shows 'consent'. No personal data is shown, as the source requires.

Caption 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.' and TV label 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' are word for word, with the same middle-dot characters, in source order (caption, then label). 'Every check-in' gathers the three routes from 03-1 to 03-4, and the three seated patients match the three slots.

Caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' and label 'NOW · A-12' are word for word, in source order. 'his' still points to Ravi, the one standing. A-12 is one of the three slots from 03-5, so the label is set up.

Caption 'A quick vitals check first.' and the nurse's 'Let's check your vitals, Ravi.' are word for word, with speaker 'nurse' as in the source, and the caption is read first. The name is justified by the check-in form and slot. 'first' sets up the doctor beat that follows. No readings are shown.

Caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' and tablet label 'RAVI · READY' are word for word, in order. 'he' refers to Ravi from 04-2. The place change to the consultation room is stated, and it sets up the greeting in 05-1.
Ananya's 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' is word for word. Her knowing his name is grounded by 'RAVI · READY' in 04-3. The question is answered in 05-2.
Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' is word for word and answers 05-1's 'what brings you in', which comes just before it. It is a routine concern with no diagnosis.

Caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' is word for word. The doctor's silent listening links Ravi's statement to her reply. (A tablet must not appear here; see the doctor-tablet issue.)
Ananya's 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' is word for word. 'your concerns' refers back to 05-2. It gives no specific treatment advice.

Meera's 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' is word for word. Welbuk Health was already set up by the 03-2 caption. The phone comes out of his pocket, where it has been since 04-1.
Ravi's 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' is word for word. 'So' draws on Meera's 06-1 statement, which comes just before it. The WELBUK HEALTH label is a supplement.
Meera's 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' is word for word. 'That' answers the 06-2 question just before it, and 'what is available' keeps the source's hedge.
Caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' is word for word. It closes the visit after the walkthrough offer.
Caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' is word for word. The conditional 'may' marks it as hypothetical.

The 'WELBUK VISION' label, which the source requires, and the caption 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' are word for word. The continuity text must point to this panel (see issues).
The repeated WELBUK VISION label is a supplement that keeps the vision framing. The caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' is word for word.
The labels 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' and the final caption 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' are word for word. The labels link back to 02-1, 02-3 and 06-2.
